article.title: NFL EDGE Sunday Evening Brief
article.dek: Sunday night is here, Mayfield is back, and Monday's only open name is Barkley.

items.headline: Tonight: Chiefs at Seahawks, 8:20 p.m. ET
paragraphs: The last Sunday game of the day is the one left on the board. Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs visit Sam Darnold and the Seahawks at 8:20 p.m. ET, and the app's QB row has both starters confirmed.

The backup picture changed at inactive time. Seattle's Drew Lock is inactive with a right elbow injury and dresses only as the emergency third quarterback, so Jalen Milroe is the No. 2 behind Darnold. Seattle does get safety Nick Emmanwori, linebacker DeMarcus Lawrence and linebacker Uchenna Nwosu back after they were listed as questionable, but running back Zach Charbonnet is out. Kansas City's Rashee Rice is inactive.
Most of Sunday's slate is already underway, so the evening board prices only tonight's game and Monday night. That is why tonight's card and Monday's number are the whole evening brief.
items.takeaway: Starters confirmed for tonight, Seattle's backup QB changed, and only tonight and Monday are left on the board.

items.headline: Injury roundup: Mayfield played, Barkley is the Monday question
paragraphs: The morning's open question is settled. Baker Mayfield returned to Tampa Bay's lineup against Carolina after three games out with a broken thumb, and he led the Bucs to a touchdown on the opening drive. The app's QB row now lists him with no injury tag.

Monday night is nearly set. The Eagles ruled out receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, linebacker Nolan Smith and defensive back Michael Carter. Dallas ruled out tackle Drew Shelton, receiver KaVontae Turpin and linebacker Dee Winters, while George Pickens and Joey Porter Jr. carry no designation.

Saquon Barkley is the one open name. He is expected to play Monday after a full Saturday practice, but he still carries the questionable tag — Monday's inactives, about 90 minutes before kickoff, are what settle it.
items.takeaway: Mayfield is back, Monday's report is settled except Barkley, and his call lands with Monday's inactives.

items.headline: Weather: clear and calm in Philadelphia on Monday night
paragraphs: Monday night in Philadelphia: clear, low around 50 degrees, rain chance 10 percent, wind NW around 6 mph.
That is a fact, not a totals edge — nothing in it argues the total either way.
items.takeaway: Clear and calm for Monday night in Philadelphia; judge the total on its own.

items.headline: Your evening cards: one play, on tonight's game
paragraphs: Hit Rate: Chiefs moneyline +138 (FanDuel), Chiefs at Seahawks. The model's win probability is 57.3 percent — that is what this card is for, the pick that looks most likely to win. The evaluator EV is +0.001, and the app lists reliability as LOW, so this is a thinner read than a normal card — it is still the most likely winner on the remaining board, not a promise.
Balanced: no play tonight. No offer on the remaining board satisfies the Balanced lane's contract, so the app shows nothing rather than forcing one.
Value: no play tonight, for the same reason. The Value lane only fires when the model's +EV play is actually there, and on tonight's and Monday's numbers it is not.
Two empty lanes are not a broken app. The lanes only speak when the contract is met, and with most of Sunday's games already underway, there are only two games left for them to speak about.
items.takeaway: Hit Rate is the only evening card, on the Chiefs. Balanced and Value stay quiet rather than force a play.

items.headline: Monday night: the model and the market still disagree
paragraphs: Cowboys at Eagles: the model's expected margin has this about a pick'em, while the market board has Dallas -4.5 at both books. Tanner McKee makes his second straight start for Philadelphia, and that gap has not moved all day.

When the model says pick'em and the market says -4.5, don't guess — run your number through Check. Tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator and returns a bet/no-bet verdict on your price. Full re-evaluation, not a blind override.
Monday game? Monday check.

items.headline: Learn the Game: buying points
paragraphs: (Hypothetical example:) Imagine your team is a 3-point favorite, and your book offers -3 at -110, but also offers -2.5 at -130. Paying that extra price to move the line half a point is called buying points.

What could it mean? That half-point matters most when the game lands exactly on the number you bought off. If your team wins by exactly 3, the -3 ticket pushes and the -2.5 ticket wins — but you paid more juice for every version of the bet, including all the ones that win or lose either way.

How to apply it: buying points is only worth it when the half-point you are buying sits on a common final margin, like 3 or 7. Before you pay up, type the exact line and price into Check and let the app tell you whether that version is worth betting.
items.takeaway: Buying points means paying extra juice to move the line — worth it only when the half-point sits on a common margin.

items.headline: Through the day: the remaining numbers did not move
paragraphs: Cowboys at Eagles is unchanged from the morning: Dallas -4.5 at both books, and the DraftKings total is still 43.5. The model's expected margin is unchanged too, about a pick'em — so the model-versus-market gap on Monday is the same gap it was this morning.

Chiefs at Seahawks is unchanged as well: Seattle -3.0 at FanDuel, with the total at 43.5 at both books. The evening board's other Sunday games show no market prices at all, because they are already underway — there is nothing left to move on them.

The card change is rotation, not a new opinion. The morning's Steelers, Browns and Raiders cards are off the board because their games kicked off, and the evening Hit Rate card is a new card on a game that is still to come. No spread flipped sides through the day.
items.takeaway: Nothing moved on the two remaining games — the card change is just games kicking off, not new market opinion.

items.headline: What didn't move — and the one timing note
paragraphs: When the board hasn't picked up a move, or your book isn't DraftKings or FanDuel, tap Check, type in your book's line and price — the app runs it back through the model and evaluator and returns a bet/no-bet verdict on your price. Full re-evaluation, not a blind override.

One timing note, and only one: the thing worth waiting for is Monday's inactives, about 90 minutes before the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff, because Barkley is the one genuinely open question left. For tonight's game, there is nothing left to wait for — it kicks off at 8:20 p.m. ET, so if your book's number works right now and Check says bet, bet now.
items.takeaway: Monday's inactives are the one thing worth waiting for; tonight's game kicks off tonight, so a good number now is the play.

items.headline: Tonight's job: two games left, check them both
paragraphs: The board refreshes every morning and evening, and tonight it holds just two games. Work through tonight's game first, since it kicks off at 8:20 p.m. ET, then set up Monday night: the model-versus-market gap on Dallas -4.5 is the number to run through Check.

One more thing, because the tracker only works if you're honest with yourself: settlement is manual, and there is no auto-settle. Log the losers too, not just the winners — that is the only way the record means anything next week.
items.takeaway: Tonight first, Monday next, Check on both — and log the losers too, because the tracker only works if the record is honest.
